places.name: Doe Library
places.blurb: Grand reading rooms under a coffered ceiling. The Morrison Library inside is the quiet favorite.

places.name: Soda Hall
places.blurb: Home of Berkeley computer science. The Wozniak Lounge is the late night study spot.

places.name: Sather Tower
places.blurb: The Campanile. Ride to the observation deck for a full view of the Bay.

places.name: Moffitt Library
places.blurb: Open late with bright study floors and a cafe by the entrance.

places.name: Sather Gate
places.blurb: The historic bronze gate between Sproul Plaza and the heart of campus.

places.name: Memorial Glade
places.blurb: The big lawn in the middle of campus. Best spot for a sunny lunch.

places.name: Hearst Mining Building
places.blurb: A Beaux-Arts atrium with skylights. Look up, then climb to the upper galleries.

places.name: Bancroft Library
places.blurb: Rare books, maps and manuscripts. Nobody on Odyssey has explored it yet.

places.name: Valley Life Sciences
places.blurb: Look for the T. rex skeleton in the atrium.

places.name: Greek Theatre
places.blurb: Open air amphitheater in the hills. Be the first explorer on the lawn seats.

places.name: Haas School of Business
places.blurb: Courtyard complex with three connected buildings and a sunny cafe.

places.name: Moe's Books
places.blurb: Four floors of new and used books on Telegraph. The rare book room upstairs is a treat.

places.name: Telegraph Avenue
places.blurb: Street vendors, records, murals and late night food south of campus.

places.name: Caffe Strada
places.blurb: The campus classic patio. Order the white chocolate mocha.

places.name: Cheese Board Pizza
places.blurb: One pizza a day and live jazz. Grab a slice and find a spot on the median.

places.name: Berkeley Art Museum
places.blurb: BAMPFA. Galleries and the film theater downtown, with a great cafe upstairs.

places.name: Berkeley Public Library
places.blurb: The Art Deco central branch downtown, with a rooftop garden.

places.name: Berkeley Rose Garden
places.blurb: Terraced amphitheater of roses facing the Golden Gate. Quiet paths everywhere.

places.name: Indian Rock Park
places.blurb: Climb the rock for the best sunset in the East Bay.

places.name: Lawrence Hall of Science
places.blurb: Hands-on science up in the hills, with a whale sculpture outside.

places.name: UC Botanical Garden
places.blurb: Over 10,000 plants in Strawberry Canyon. The cactus garden is a must.

places.name: Berkeley Bowl
places.blurb: A legendary produce market. Do not skip the bakery aisle.

places.name: Berkeley Marina
places.blurb: Kites, sailboats and the pier walk along the shoreline.

places.name: Tilden Regional Park
places.blurb: Lake Anza, the steam trains and miles of trails.

places.name: Y Combinator
places.blurb: The startup accelerator in the old Union Iron Works office at Pier 70.

places.name: Pier 70
places.blurb: A historic shipyard turning into a new waterfront neighborhood. Brick machine shops, cranes and open plazas.

places.name: Crane Cove Park
places.blurb: A bayfront park with a small beach, two restored shipyard cranes and a boat launch.

places.name: Esprit Park
places.blurb: Dogpatch's neighborhood lawn, ringed by tall trees. Busy with dogs before work and picnics at lunch.

places.name: Piccino
places.blurb: The yellow corner cafe for espresso, pastries and wood fired pizza. Grab the patio if you can.

places.name: Paper Son Coffee
places.blurb: Coffee on Third Street a block from YC, with a quiet back room for laptops.

places.name: Long Bridge Pizza
places.blurb: Neighborhood pizza by the slice next door to Paper Son.

places.name: Dogpatch Saloon
places.blurb: A century old bar with a wood stove and live jazz on Sundays.

places.name: Just for You Cafe
places.blurb: Big breakfasts and beignets on 22nd Street.

places.name: Dogpatch Boulders
places.blurb: A bouldering gym in an old warehouse with a busy main wall.

places.name: Minnesota Street Project
places.blurb: Contemporary art galleries in converted warehouses.

places.name: 22nd Street Station
places.blurb: The Caltrain stop for Dogpatch, up the stairs from 22nd Street.

places.name: Potrero Hill Rec Center
places.blurb: Ball fields and one of the best skyline views in the city from the top of the hill.

places.name: Warm Water Cove
places.blurb: A small, quiet park at the end of 24th Street, right on the water.

places.name: The Ramp
places.blurb: A waterfront bar and grill by the boatyard with a big deck over the bay.

places.name: Chase Center
places.blurb: Home of the Warriors, plus concerts and a plaza full of food.

places.name: UCSF Mission Bay
places.blurb: A research campus with open plazas between the labs.

places.name: Mission Creek Park
places.blurb: A path along the creek past the houseboats, with kayaks on calm days.

places.name: Oracle Park
places.blurb: The Giants' ballpark on the bay, with the walkway along McCovey Cove.

places.name: ICA San Francisco
places.blurb: A free contemporary art museum in an old Dogpatch warehouse, with big rotating shows.

places.name: Museum of Craft and Design
places.blurb: Small museum of modern craft and design, plus a design shop worth the stop.

places.name: Hard Knox Cafe
places.blurb: Soul food classics: fried chicken, waffles and greens in a cozy tin-roofed room.

places.name: Serpentine
places.blurb: Bright neighborhood restaurant in a converted warehouse, known for weekend brunch.

places.name: Smokestack at Magnolia
places.blurb: Texas style barbecue and house-brewed beer in a big old industrial hall.

places.name: Third Rail
places.blurb: Dim cocktail bar with house jerky, steps from Third Street.

places.name: Neighbor Bakehouse
places.blurb: Tiny bakery with a line for its croissants and morning buns.

places.name: Recchiuti theLab
places.blurb: Recchiuti's chocolate lab and cafe, with truffles, s'mores and hot chocolate.

places.name: Dogpatch WineWorks
places.blurb: Urban winery and tasting room in a brick warehouse.

places.name: Uber Headquarters
places.blurb: Uber's glass towers in Mission Bay, linked by sky bridges over a public plaza.

places.name: Dropbox at The Exchange
places.blurb: The Exchange, Dropbox's Mission Bay campus, with terraces facing the bay.

places.name: Piccino Coffee Bar
places.blurb: Bright corner coffee bar from the Piccino team, with pastries and a retail wall.

people.name: Nina Park

people.name: Jordan Ellis
people.bio: Coffee first, then wherever the day goes.

people.name: Priya Raman
people.bio: Bookstores, botanical gardens and slow Sundays.

people.name: Sam Okafor
people.bio: Trail runner. If there is a hill, I am on it.

people.name: Hana Sato
people.bio: Architecture nerd. I collect beautiful buildings.

people.name: Diego Reyes
people.bio: Atlas tier. Ask me where the best tacos are.

people.name: Marco Silva
people.bio: Food lover, five star cafe hunter.

explorers.name: Ibn Battuta
explorers.known: Traveled for about 30 years across North and West Africa, the Middle East, India and China, roughly 117,000 km.
explorers.trait: Long journeys and lots of new cities

explorers.name: Zheng He
explorers.known: Led seven large Ming fleet voyages to Southeast Asia, India, Arabia and the East African coast.

explorers.name: Xuanzang
explorers.known: A monk and scholar who walked from China to India and back over about 17 years, bringing home hundreds of texts.
explorers.trait: Libraries, study spots and quiet places

explorers.name: Ida Pfeiffer
explorers.known: One of the first women to travel around the world solo, twice, and wrote bestselling travel journals.
explorers.trait: Solo trips and writing it all down

explorers.name: Nellie Bly
explorers.known: A journalist who raced around the world in 72 days in 1889 and 1890, beating a fictional record.
explorers.trait: Fast paced days with many stops

explorers.name: Matthew Henson
explorers.known: Arctic explorer and navigator on the 1909 expedition that reported reaching the North Pole.

explorers.name: Ynes Mexia
explorers.known: Botanist who studied at UC Berkeley and collected around 145,000 plant specimens across Mexico and South America.

explorers.name: Amelia Earhart
explorers.known: Aviation pioneer and the first woman to fly solo across the Atlantic, in 1932.

explorers.name: Tenzing Norgay
explorers.known: Sherpa mountaineer who reached the summit of Everest with Edmund Hillary in 1953.

explorers.name: Junko Tabei
explorers.known: First woman to summit Everest, in 1975, and the first woman to climb the Seven Summits.

explorers.name: Jacques Cousteau
explorers.known: Ocean explorer who co-developed the Aqua-Lung and brought the undersea world to film.
explorers.trait: Waterfronts and places few people see

posts.caption: Soda Hall after dark is a whole vibe. Walkthrough is up for anyone heading to office hours.
First on Odyssey at the Cheese Board. Recorded the line so you know where to stand.
Heyns Reading Room never gets old.
Walked the whole base of the Campanile. Elevator is around the back.
That atrium. Recorded the ground floor, the galleries upstairs are worth it.
Cactus garden in full sun.
Morning fuel before the hills.
Lake Anza loop in the morning fog. 2.1 km and nobody else around.
Late night on Telegraph.
Made it to the top of the Campanile.
Sunset from Indian Rock. Worth every one of those stairs.
Five stars. The line was worth it.

110 places later. California, you're next.
My name is on Hearst Mining for good.
Pathfinder unlocked. Tokyo is calling.
Thirty days, thirty trails.
Five campus buildings explored.
Caffe Strada is basically my office.
Southside food crawl. Six stops, zero regrets.
Garden day with the hills to myself.
